source_title: Nausicaä of the Valley of the Wind
continuity_scope: Nausicaä of the Valley of the Wind, Vol. 1, VIZ paperback edition (Studio Ghibli Library imprint; 136 pages; ISBN 978-1-59116-408-1; released 2004-02-11). This is a narrow publisher-metadata pass for that manga volume only. The 1984 theatrical film, guidebooks, games, later manga volumes, Japanese witnesses, translations, and adaptations are separate and excluded.

coverage_rule: Include only individual dramatic characters directly named and described in VIZ's selected Volume 1 synopsis. That synopsis names and describes Nausicaä only; she is recorded. No broader cast, relationship, or primary-panel pass is claimed because no accessible page- or chapter-level manga locator was available in the selected evidence.
omissions: All other Volume 1 people, whose names or claim-specific descriptions lack accessible locators in the selected publisher metadata.
Ohmu and other creatures as individual character nodes; creature categories remain terms/dimensions unless a named individual is directly evidenced.
Peoples, factions, aircraft, artifacts, toxic ecology, places, powers, and themes as character nodes.
The 1984 film, guidebooks, games, later manga, Japanese editions, translations, and other adaptations.
content_cautions: The selected synopsis explicitly frames conflict among empires over remaining natural resources. It does not provide a scene-level inventory of war violence, injury, ecological illness, disability, or bodily harm; this pass makes no further claim.
Empathic connection to animals and insects is a fictional premise. It is not mapped to real-world disability, illness, animal communication, Indigenous or other living cultural practice.
The available Volume 1 metadata does not document cultural inspirations; no real-world people, nation, ethnicity, or tradition equivalence is assigned.
uncertainties: No accessible primary page/panel or chapter locator was available for the selected VIZ Volume 1 product, so all character claims remain synopsis-level official-reference claims.
VIZ's accessible product page credits Hayao Miyazaki for story and art but does not identify an individual English translator; none is inferred.
The product synopsis does not establish detailed toxic-ecology mechanics, disease/illness, aircraft, artifacts, factions, places, political offices, or the full scope of Nausicaä's abilities.
Manga and 1984 film continuity details are not merged; the Studio Ghibli page is used only to identify the film as a separate work.
evidence_basis: VIZ's official Volume 1 product page supplies all selected-manga character, ecological-conflict, and bibliographic claims. Studio Ghibli's official film page confirms that the 1984 theatrical film is a distinct work and is used solely to retain the continuity boundary. No fan wiki or Wikipedia was used.
